feature_name: Default interactive picker launch
user_story: As a user, I want to run `resume` with no flags so that I get an interactive fuzzy picker of my coding-agent sessions in the current Scope.
expected_behaviour: When neither `--list` nor `--json` is passed, `app::run` calls `run_interactive`, which spawns one discovery thread per configured agent, streams candidates into the Skim picker via a bounded channel, and returns the picker's exit code (src/app.rs:108-129, run_interactive at src/app.rs:234-308).
how_to_test: cd into a directory with known pi/claude/codex/omp session fixtures and run `resume` with no arguments in a real terminal; observe the Skim picker opens with streamed rows.

feature_name: Optional positional directory argument
user_story: As a user, I want to pass a directory path as the first positional argument so that Scope is derived from that directory instead of my current working directory.
expected_behaviour: `Cli.directory: Option<PathBuf>` (src/cli.rs:254) is used by `build_scope` as `cli.directory.as_deref().unwrap_or(Path::new("."))` then canonicalized via `scope::canonical_base` (src/app.rs:170-171). A nonexistent directory causes `canonical_base` to fail and `run` prints `resume: <error>` and returns EXIT_USAGE (2) (src/app.rs:111-116).
how_to_test: Run `resume /path/to/other/worktree --list` and confirm sessions are scoped to that worktree, not cwd; run `resume /nonexistent/path` and confirm exit code 2 with an error message.

feature_name: -U/--up <N|all> explicit upward Scope
user_story: As a user, I want `--up N` so that Scope includes my current directory and up to N ancestor directories, overriding the Git default.
expected_behaviour: `Cli.up: Option<Distance>` parses `N` or `all` via `Distance::FromStr` (src/cli.rs:6-24 (FromStr body at 14-23; error string now sourced from errors::E1003.parser_message() at cli.rs:21)). When set, `build_scope` builds `Direction::Up(distance)` and Scope mode becomes `ScopeMode::Up`, whose `contains` checks `self.base.ancestors().position(...)` is within distance (src/scope.rs (ScopeMode::Up match arm)).
how_to_test: In a nested directory tree `/a/b/c`, run `resume --up 1` from `/a/b/c` and confirm sessions from `/a/b/c` and `/a/b` are included but not `/a` or `/a/b/c/d`.

feature_name: --up all upward Scope to filesystem root
user_story: As a user, I want `--up all` so that every ancestor directory up to `/` is in Scope.
expected_behaviour: `Distance::All` makes `within()` always return true for Up mode (src/scope.rs:114-119), so `contains` matches any ancestor of base regardless of distance, per the table-driven test `up all root` (src/scope.rs:229-234).
how_to_test: Run `resume --up all` deep inside a directory tree and confirm sessions recorded anywhere from cwd up through `/` appear, but no descendant/sibling sessions do.

feature_name: -D/--down <N|all> explicit downward Scope
user_story: As a user, I want `--down N` so that Scope includes my current directory and descendants up to N path-component edges deep.
expected_behaviour: `Cli.down: Option<Distance>` mirrors `--up`; Scope mode `ScopeMode::Down` uses `candidate.real_path.strip_prefix(&self.base)` and checks the suffix's component count is within distance (src/scope.rs:94-98); depth-2 example verified by `down two` test (src/scope.rs:249-254).
how_to_test: From a directory with subdirectories 2+ levels deep containing sessions, run `resume --down 2 --list` and confirm only sessions at depth <=2 are listed.

feature_name: --down all downward Scope to every descendant
user_story: As a user, I want `--down all` so that every descendant directory of my current directory is in Scope, including at `/` which is intentionally broad.
expected_behaviour: `Distance::All` in Down mode always satisfies `within()` (src/scope.rs:114-119); README explicitly documents that `--down all` at `/` is broad but still directory-derived, not machine-wide (README.md Explicit direction section).
how_to_test: Run `resume --down all` from a shallow directory containing many nested session workspaces and confirm all of them appear regardless of depth.

feature_name: --up and --down are mutually exclusive
user_story: As a user, I want the CLI to reject combining `--up` and `--down` so that I get a clear usage error instead of ambiguous behavior.
expected_behaviour: `#[arg(... conflicts_with = "down")]` on `up` and `#[arg(... conflicts_with = "confirm_always"... )]`-style `conflicts_with = "up"` on `down` (src/cli.rs:256-274 (up conflicts_with at 260, down at 270)) makes clap reject the combination with exit code 2, tested by `direction_conflict_is_usage_error` (src/cli.rs:424).
how_to_test: Run `resume --up 1 --down 2` and confirm clap prints a usage error and exits with code 2.

feature_name: Invalid --up/--down value is a usage error
user_story: As a user, I want a non-numeric, non-'all' value (or a negative number) for `--up`/`--down` to be rejected clearly so that I know I made a typo.
expected_behaviour: `Distance::from_str` returns `Err("expected a non-negative integer or 'all'")` for anything but `all` (case-insensitive) or a parseable non-negative integer (src/cli.rs:14-23 (returns errors::E1003.parser_message() at cli.rs:21)); clap surfaces this as exit code 2, tested by `invalid_distance_is_usage_error` (src/cli.rs:437 (test renamed/merged: invalid_distance_and_since_are_usage_errors)).
how_to_test: Run `resume --up -1` and confirm exit code 2 with a usage error mentioning a non-negative integer or 'all'.
error_notes: Phase 4 independently re-ran the exact `resume --up -1` repro against the freshly built release binary in an isolated environment: exit 2 with `expected a non-negative integer or 'all'`; Phase 3 fix confirmed.

feature_name: -a/--agent is repeatable and replaces, not extends, the agent list
user_story: As a user, I want repeated `-a pi -a codex` flags to set the exact agent list used for discovery so that I can narrow which integrations run.
expected_behaviour: `Cli.agent: Vec<OsString>` uses `action = clap::ArgAction::Append` (src/cli.rs:276-282 (ArgAction::Append)); `effective_options` only falls back to config/defaults when `cli.agent.is_empty()`, otherwise uses exactly the CLI-supplied list (src/app.rs:134-150), tested by `repeated_agent_preserves_replacement_list` (src/cli.rs:516).
how_to_test: Run `resume -a pi -a codex --list` and confirm only pi and codex sessions appear even if config.toml lists all four agents.

feature_name: Unknown agent name in -a/--agent is a usage error
user_story: As a user, I want `resume -a bogus` to fail clearly so that I know 'bogus' is not a supported agent name.
expected_behaviour: `effective_options` checks each agent against `matches!(agent.as_str(), "pi" | "claude" | "codex" | "omp")` and returns `Err(format!("unknown agent {agent:?}"))` if not, causing `run` to print `resume: unknown agent "bogus"` and return EXIT_USAGE (2) (src/app.rs:135-150 (unknown-agent check at 147-148), src/app.rs:107-108), tested by `unknown_agent_is_usage_error` (src/app.rs:917-931) and the integration test `no_sessions_is_success_and_invalid_agent_is_usage_error` (tests/step9_app.rs:157).
how_to_test: Run `resume --list --agent bogus` and confirm exit code 2 and stderr containing `unknown agent "bogus"`.

feature_name: -a/--agent values are lowercased before validation
user_story: As a user, I want `-a PI` or `-a Codex` to work the same as lowercase so that casing mistakes don't cause failures.
expected_behaviour: `effective_options` maps each `OsString` agent via `.to_string_lossy().to_ascii_lowercase()` before validation (src/app.rs:139 (.to_string_lossy().to_ascii_lowercase())).
how_to_test: Run `resume -a PI --list` and confirm it behaves identically to `resume -a pi --list`.

feature_name: --list mode: stable text listing
user_story: As a user, I want `--list` so that discovery completes fully and I get one deterministic terminal-safe text row per session, suitable for scripting or piping.
expected_behaviour: When `cli.list` is true, `run` calls `discover_all` (blocking until every integration thread joins), prints diagnostics to stderr, then `print_list` prints one `picker_candidate(...).display` line per session in `print_list` (src/app.rs:108-129, src/app.rs:856 (print_list)); sessions are pre-sorted deterministically by `compare_sessions` inside `discover_all` (src/app.rs:170-171).
how_to_test: Run `resume --list` in a directory with known sessions and confirm stable, deterministically ordered rows are printed to stdout with no interactive UI.

feature_name: --json mode: machine-readable v1 output
user_story: As a user, I want `--json` so that I get one machine-parseable JSON document on stdout describing sessions and errors, safe to pipe into `jq`.
expected_behaviour: When `cli.json` is true, `run` calls `discover_all` then `print_json`, which serializes a `JsonOutput { schemaVersion: 1, sessions, errors }` via `serde_json::to_string` and prints exactly one line to stdout (src/app.rs:108-129, src/app.rs:814 (print_json)).
how_to_test: Run `resume --json 2>/dev/null | jq .` and confirm exactly one valid JSON document with schemaVersion 1 is printed.

feature_name: --list and --json share the same discover_all path and exit-code logic
user_story: As a user, I want `--list` and `--json` to apply identical Scope/agent filtering and identical exit-code rules so that only the output format differs.
expected_behaviour: Both branches call `discover_all(&options, scope)` then `discovery_exit(&records, &state)` (src/app.rs:108-129); only the printer (`print_list` vs `print_json`) differs.
how_to_test: Run `resume --list --agent pi` and `resume --json --agent pi` in the same directory and confirm the same session set (by id) appears in both, only formatted differently.

feature_name: --verbose enables verbose diagnostics
user_story: As a user, I want `--verbose` so that stderr diagnostics include a redacted source path and error chain, not just a category and count.
expected_behaviour: `Cli.verbose: bool` (src/cli.rs:296) is ORed with `config.verbose` in `effective_options` (src/app.rs (effective_options verbose field)) and threaded to `print_diagnostics(&state, options.verbose)`; `render_diagnostic` appends `redact_path(path)` and `redact_text(chain)` only when `verbose` is true (src/app.rs:872 (print_diagnostics) / 933-951 (render_diagnostic)).
how_to_test: Create a fixture with an intentionally malformed session file, run `resume --list` (no diagnostic path shown) then `resume --verbose --list` (diagnostic path/chain shown), and diff stderr output.

feature_name: --config <PATH> explicit config file path
user_story: As a user, I want `--config /path/to/config.toml` so that I can point resume at a specific configuration file, bypassing XDG/home discovery.
expected_behaviour: `Cli.config: Option<PathBuf>` (src/cli.rs:298) is passed to `crate::config::load(cli.config.clone())`; `discover_path` returns the explicit path immediately if `Some`, without checking existence (src/config.rs:67-81 (discover_path)), tested by `explicit_then_xdg_then_home_precedence` (src/config.rs:112 (explicit_then_xdg_then_home_precedence)).
how_to_test: Write a config.toml at a nonstandard path and run `resume --config /that/path/config.toml config example`-style check, or run `resume --config /that/path/config.toml --list` and confirm its `agents` field is honored.

feature_name: --confirm-always requests confirmation for every Resume
user_story: As a user, I want `--confirm-always` so that I am prompted to confirm before resuming any session, even a normal-risk one.
expected_behaviour: `Cli.confirm_always: bool` (src/cli.rs:300-305) is ORed with `config.confirm_always` in `effective_options` (src/app.rs:162); `launch::should_confirm` returns true whenever `confirm_always && !no_confirm`, and `launch::risk_reasons` adds a synthetic "confirmation requested" reason when otherwise risk-free (src/launch.rs (risk_reasons/should_confirm), src/launch.rs (risk_reasons)).
how_to_test: Select a normal-risk session via the picker with `resume --confirm-always` and confirm the 'Continue? [y/N]' prompt appears even though the session has no risk flags.

feature_name: --no-confirm suppresses ordinary confirmation only
user_story: As a user, I want `--no-confirm` so that I skip the ordinary confirmation prompt, but I still want to be warned before resuming a genuinely risky session.
expected_behaviour: `should_confirm` computes `risky || (confirm_always && !no_confirm)` (src/launch.rs (should_confirm)): `no_confirm` only cancels the `confirm_always` branch, never the `risky` branch, so risk prompts (Active/BroadWorkspace/WorkspaceChanged/ConflictingMetadata) always still fire, tested by `no_confirm_never_bypasses_risk` (src/launch.rs:229 (no_confirm_never_bypasses_risk)).
how_to_test: Select a session flagged BroadWorkspace (workspace == $HOME or /) via `resume --no-confirm` and confirm the risk confirmation prompt still appears despite --no-confirm.

feature_name: --confirm-always and --no-confirm are mutually exclusive
user_story: As a user, I want the CLI to reject combining `--confirm-always` and `--no-confirm` since they express contradictory intents.
expected_behaviour: `#[arg(long, conflicts_with = "no_confirm")]` on `confirm_always` and the reciprocal on `no_confirm` (src/cli.rs:300-311 (confirm_always conflicts_with at 302, no_confirm at 308)) make clap reject the combination with exit code 2, tested by `confirmation_conflict_is_usage_error` (src/cli.rs:112,118-122... actually src/cli.rs 'confirmation_conflict_is_usage_error' test).
how_to_test: Run `resume --confirm-always --no-confirm` and confirm exit code 2 with a clap usage error.

feature_name: --since <duration> filters Sessions by recent activity (relative)
user_story: As a user with many old sessions, I want `--since 7d` to show only Sessions active in the last 7 days, so that I don't have to scroll past stale entries.
expected_behaviour: `Since::from_str` parses `<N><unit>` where unit is m/h/d/w (src/cli.rs, delegating to `crate::time::parse_relative_duration`); `effective_options` resolves it to a cutoff `SystemTime` via `Since::cutoff(now)` (src/app.rs:427 session_at_or_after); `discover_agent` retains only records whose transcript file mtime is at or after the cutoff via `session_at_or_after` (src/app.rs:427 session_at_or_after), applied identically in both `--list`/`--json` and the interactive picker code paths.
how_to_test: Create fixture transcripts for two+ agents, backdate one set of files' mtimes by 1 hour via `File::set_times`, run `resume --json --since 10m` and confirm only recently-modified sessions appear; covered by `since_duration_filters_out_stale_transcripts_across_all_four_agents` in tests/step9_app.rs.

feature_name: config example subcommand prints a complete example TOML
user_story: As a user, I want `resume config example` so that I can see every documented config field and its default in valid TOML, ready to copy into my config file.
expected_behaviour: `Command::Config(ConfigArgs { command: ConfigCommand::Example })` is matched in main.rs before `app::run` is ever called; `resume::cli::config_example()` returns a static string literal listing `agents`, `confirm_always`, `preview`, `preview_position`, `verbose` (src/cli.rs:375-383, src/main.rs:17-18 (Command::Config dispatch)).
how_to_test: Run `resume config example` and confirm the printed TOML matches the fields documented in README.md's Configuration section and parses successfully via `resume --config <(that output)`.

feature_name: completions bash subcommand
user_story: As a user, I want `resume completions bash` so that I can install shell completion for bash.
expected_behaviour: `Command::Completions { shell: Shell::Bash }` calls `clap_complete::generate(shells::Bash, ...)` to stdout before `app::run` executes, so it never loads config or discovers sessions (src/main.rs:19-26 (Completions match, Bash at 22), docs/completions.md).
how_to_test: Run `resume completions bash` and confirm a valid bash completion script is printed to stdout with no config/discovery side effects (verify no XDG/HOME env access needed by running with HOME unset).

feature_name: completions zsh subcommand
user_story: As a user, I want `resume completions zsh` so that I can install shell completion for zsh.
expected_behaviour: `Shell::Zsh` branch calls `generate(shells::Zsh, ...)` (src/main.rs:23 (Zsh generate)); same pre-`app::run` dispatch guarantee as bash.
how_to_test: Run `resume completions zsh` and confirm a valid zsh `_resume` completion function is printed.

feature_name: completions fish subcommand
user_story: As a user, I want `resume completions fish` so that I can install shell completion for fish.
expected_behaviour: `Shell::Fish` branch calls `generate(shells::Fish, ...)` (src/main.rs:24 (Fish generate)); subcommand parsing itself tested by `subcommands_parse` (src/cli.rs:522 (subcommands_parse)).
how_to_test: Run `resume completions fish` and confirm a valid fish completion script is printed.

feature_name: Completions/config subcommands dispatch before app startup
user_story: As a user, I want `resume completions bash` and `resume config example` to work even with no HOME, no config file, and no session data present, so that packaging/CI can generate completions safely.
expected_behaviour: `main()` matches `cli.command` for `Config`/`Completions` and returns before ever calling `resume::app::run(cli)` (src/main.rs:8-27 (app::run only reached in the None arm at line 27)); docs/completions.md explicitly states these subcommands 'do not load a config file, derive Scope, or discover/scan Sessions'.
how_to_test: Run `env -i resume completions bash` (fully cleared environment) and confirm it still succeeds and prints a script, with no error about missing HOME or config.

feature_name: Default Scope inside a Git repository includes all worktrees
user_story: As a user working inside a Git repo, I want the default Scope (no --up/--down) to include every Workspace in the main repo and all linked worktrees at any depth, so that I see sessions from any of my worktrees.
expected_behaviour: `build_scope` calls `discover_git_scope(&base)`; on success it builds `DefaultScope::Git { common_dir, worktrees }`, and `Scope::contains` in `ScopeMode::Git` accepts any candidate whose real path starts with one of `worktrees`, rejecting a candidate whose `git_common_dir` differs (nested repo) (src/app.rs:170-191 (build_scope), src/scope.rs:102-117 (ScopeMode::Git match arm)), tested by `git_scope_includes_main_linked_and_deep_but_excludes_nested_repo` (src/scope.rs:417 (git_scope_includes_main_linked_and_deep_but_excludes_nested_repo)).
how_to_test: Inside a repo with a linked worktree via `git worktree add`, run `resume --list` from either worktree and confirm sessions recorded under both worktrees appear, while a nested unrelated git repo's sessions are excluded.
error_notes: Verified against target/release/resume in a real repository with a linked worktree and a nested independently initialized repository: MAIN and LINKED remained listed while NESTED was excluded. Live Workspace candidates now resolve their Git common directory before Git Scope matching. Phase 4 independently re-verified against freshly built target/release/resume; isolated real-binary fixtures and the full locked all-features suite matched expected behavior.

feature_name: Default Scope outside Git is the exact current directory only
user_story: As a user working outside any Git repository, I want the default Scope to be just my current real directory, not its children, so that I don't see unrelated sessions.
expected_behaviour: When `discover_git_scope` fails (not a repo), `build_scope` sets `DefaultScope::Exact { git_warning: Some(error) }`, giving `ScopeMode::Exact`, whose `contains` requires `candidate.real_path == self.base` exactly (src/app.rs:183-188 (DefaultScope::Exact fallback), src/scope.rs:91 (ScopeMode::Exact)), tested by `non_git_fallback_is_exact_and_missing_workspace_is_matched_by_last_known_path` (src/scope.rs:443) — corrected test name; the CSV previously cited a nonexistent test name.
how_to_test: Run `resume --list` from a plain (non-git) directory containing a session subdirectory and confirm only sessions whose recorded Workspace is exactly that directory appear, not a session in a subdirectory.
error_notes: Phase 4 independently re-verified against freshly built target/release/resume; isolated real-binary fixtures and the full locked all-features suite matched expected behavior.

feature_name: Git Scope discovery failure is reported, falls back to exact Scope
user_story: As a user, I want a Git failure (e.g. corrupted repo, git binary missing) to degrade gracefully to exact-directory Scope rather than crashing resume.
expected_behaviour: RESOLVED (was flagged as a doc/behavior gap; now fixed and test-backed). `discover_git_scope` errors become `DefaultScope::Exact { git_warning: Some(error.to_string()) }` (src/app.rs:178-185, build_scope). That warning IS surfaced as a `Diagnostic` of category `git_scope_discovery_failed` via `scope_warning_diagnostic` (src/app.rs:668-675), injected into `DiscoveryState.errors` in BOTH `discover_all` (src/app.rs:199) and `run_interactive` (src/app.rs:240), and printed to stderr by `print_diagnostics`/`aggregate_diagnostics` (src/app.rs:872,892). The category maps to E3002 GIT_SCOPE_DISCOVERY_FAILED in the unified error catalog (src/errors.rs) and is documented at src/man.rs:38,517. README.md:50 ('A Git failure is reported as a diagnostic.') is now accurate.
how_to_test: Simulate `git` being unavailable (e.g. temporarily rename it off PATH) inside a git repo, run `resume --list`, and confirm resume falls back to exact-directory Scope while stderr shows `resume: git_scope_discovery_failed: 1` (and, with --verbose, the underlying error text). Unit-covered by `git_scope_failure_becomes_a_visible_diagnostic` (src/app.rs:1124), which asserts category, count, non-verbose rendering, and verbose rendering.
error_notes: Fix confirmed by 3 independent domain audits (Scope/Config, CLI, Safety/Doccheck agents) reading current src/app.rs. Dedicated E2E coverage added: git_unavailable_falls_back_to_exact_scope_with_a_visible_diagnostic (tests/step9_app.rs) runs the real binary with `--list --agent pi` (PATH has no git, by construction of run_with_env), asserts 'git_scope_discovery_failed' on stderr AND that the exact-directory fallback still finds the pi session on stdout.

feature_name: Directory Distance 0 means exactly the current directory
user_story: As a user, I want `--up 0` or `--down 0` to mean exactly the current real directory, matching neither parent nor child.
expected_behaviour: `within(&Distance::Finite(0), edges)` is true only when `edges <= 0`, i.e. `edges == 0`; verified by the table-driven cases `up zero self`/`up zero parent`/`down zero self`/`down zero child` (src/scope.rs:182-186 (fn within)).
how_to_test: Run `resume --up 0 --list` and `resume --down 0 --list` from a directory with a session recorded exactly there and confirm both include it, while a parent-recorded or child-recorded session is excluded.
error_notes: Phase 4 independently re-verified against freshly built target/release/resume; isolated real-binary fixtures and the full locked all-features suite matched expected behavior.

feature_name: Scope base and Workspace candidates are canonicalized (symlinks resolved)
user_story: As a user, I want resume to compare real (symlink-resolved) paths so that a symlinked path to my project matches sessions recorded under the real path.
expected_behaviour: `canonical_base` calls `path.canonicalize()` (src/scope.rs:189-191 (canonical_base)), and `canonical_workspace` does the same for candidate workspaces (src/scope.rs:193-195 (canonical_workspace)), tested by `canonicalization_resolves_symlinks_and_rejects_missing` (src/scope.rs:561 (canonicalization_resolves_symlinks_and_rejects_missing)).
how_to_test: Create a symlink to a workspace directory, cd through the symlink, and run `resume --list`; confirm sessions recorded under the real (non-symlink) path are still matched.
error_notes: Phase 4 independently re-verified against freshly built target/release/resume; isolated real-binary fixtures and the full locked all-features suite matched expected behavior.

feature_name: A missing/nonexistent base directory is a usage error
user_story: As a user, I want a clear error if I pass a directory that does not exist so that I don't get a confusing crash.
expected_behaviour: `canonical_base` returns `Err` when `path.canonicalize()` fails on a missing directory; `build_scope`'s caller in `run` prints `resume: <error>` and returns `EXIT_USAGE` (2) (src/app.rs:111-116 (run build_scope error arm) + src/app.rs:171 (canonical_base call) + src/scope.rs:189-191 (canonical_base impl)).
how_to_test: Run `resume /this/path/does/not/exist` and confirm exit code 2 with a clear error message.
error_notes: Phase 4 independently re-verified against freshly built target/release/resume; isolated real-binary fixtures and the full locked all-features suite matched expected behavior.

feature_name: A Session whose recorded Workspace no longer exists is diagnosed as Unavailable, not resumable
user_story: As a user, I want sessions whose recorded directory was deleted or moved to still be listed for diagnosis, but marked Unavailable so I can't accidentally resume into a broken path.
expected_behaviour: `normalize_availability` sets `session.support = SupportStatus::Unavailable` whenever `session.workspace.workspace().is_none_or(|p| !p.is_dir())` (src/app.rs:657-660 (normalize_availability)), applied after every integration's discovery (src/app.rs:464,490,537,606 (per-agent call sites)); `status_label` renders it as `UNAVAILABLE` (src/app.rs:766-783 (status_label, UNAVAILABLE arm at 781)).
how_to_test: Discover a session, then delete its recorded workspace directory, re-run `resume --list`, and confirm the session still appears with status UNAVAILABLE and cannot be selected for resume.
error_notes: Verified against target/release/resume --down all --list --agent pi after deleting a recorded Workspace: the Session remained listed with UNAVAILABLE. Missing Workspaces are matched by their last-known real path (canonical existing ancestor plus missing suffix), while genuinely out-of-scope paths remain excluded. Phase 4 independently re-verified against freshly built target/release/resume; isolated real-binary fixtures and the full locked all-features suite matched expected behavior.

feature_name: --config explicit path has highest precedence
user_story: As a user, I want an explicit `--config <PATH>` to always win over XDG/home discovery, even if the path doesn't exist yet.
expected_behaviour: `discover_path` returns `explicit` immediately whenever `Some`, before checking XDG or home (src/config.rs:67-70 (discover_path explicit return)), tested by `explicit_then_xdg_then_home_precedence` (src/config.rs:112 (explicit_then_xdg_then_home_precedence)); if the explicit file doesn't exist, `load_path` will fail with `ConfigError::Read` when actually loading (src/config.rs:99-107 (load_path)).
how_to_test: Set XDG_CONFIG_HOME and HOME to point at valid config files with different `agents` lists, then run `resume --config /third/path/config.toml --list` and confirm the third file's settings apply (or a read error if it doesn't exist).

feature_name: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/resume/config.toml precedence over home
user_story: As a user, I want my XDG_CONFIG_HOME config to be used when present, ahead of the ~/.config fallback.
expected_behaviour: `discover_path` checks `xdg.join("resume/config.toml")` via the injected `exists` predicate and returns it if present, before falling back to `home.join(".config/resume/config.toml")` (src/config.rs:71-78 (discover_path xdg check)), tested by `explicit_then_xdg_then_home_precedence` (src/config.rs:112 (explicit_then_xdg_then_home_precedence)).
how_to_test: Create both `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/resume/config.toml` and `~/.config/resume/config.toml` with different `agents` lists, run `resume --list` with no `--config`, and confirm the XDG file's settings apply.

feature_name: ~/.config/resume/config.toml is used only when XDG config is absent

feature_name: Exactly one config file is loaded; files are never merged
user_story: As a user, I want resume to load a single config file deterministically rather than silently merging multiple sources, so config behavior is predictable.

feature_name: Unknown TOML fields are rejected
user_story: As a user, I want a typo'd config field (e.g. from an old or unsupported option) to fail loudly rather than being silently ignored.
expected_behaviour: `Config` derives `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` (src/config.rs:36 (#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)])), so any field not in {agents, confirm_always, preview, preview_position, verbose} causes `toml::from_str` to fail, surfaced as `ConfigError::Parse`, tested by `unknown_and_invalid_fields_are_rejected` for `mystery = true` (src/config.rs:136-152 (unknown_and_invalid_fields_are_rejected) + :158 (parse_error_message_includes_line_and_field_detail)).

feature_name: Invalid enum/type values in config are rejected

expected_behaviour: `PreviewMode`/`PreviewPosition` derive `Deserialize` with `#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]` and only accept `hidden`/`visible` or `auto`/`right`/`bottom` respectively (src/config.rs:22-25 (PreviewMode), :29-33 (PreviewPosition)); an invalid value like `preview_position = 'left'` fails `toml::from_str`, tested by `unknown_and_invalid_fields_are_rejected` (src/config.rs:136-152 (unknown_and_invalid_fields_are_rejected)).

feature_name: Config-level 'since' field accepts the same duration|date|all syntax as --since
user_story: As a user, I want to set a default `since` cutoff in config.toml so I don't have to pass --since on every invocation, and have --since on the CLI override it when I do.
expected_behaviour: `Config.since: Option<Since>` deserializes via `deserialize_since`, reusing `Since::from_str` so config and CLI accept identical syntax and reject the same malformed inputs (src/config.rs); `effective_options` prefers `cli.since` over `config.since` when both are present (src/app.rs), mirroring the -a/--agent override pattern.

NOT ALL exit-2 paths use the catalog — unknown-agent and missing-directory still print bare messages (E1005/E3004 reserved-not-wired by design).

feature_name: Pi session title precedence: session_info.name, else summary of first human message

feature_name: Claude transcripts with no embedded sessionId: DiscoverOnly with cwd, skipped without

feature_name: Claude resume_spec fails cleanly when there's no recorded workspace

error_notes: Corrected 2026-08-11 (parallel real-execution QA sweep): prior text described S6 as an open/HOWEVER gap; it was fixed by commit 7921808 (already present in git history before this session started). `claude_missing_workspace_diagnostic_surfaces_instead_of_being_silently_discarded` (tests/step9_app.rs) passes.

feature_name: Codex SQLite enrichment (feature-gated) can fill missing title and activity time, never overriding JSONL identity
user_story: As a Codex user who has enabled the codex-sqlite feature, I want richer titles/activity timestamps for sessions whose rollout JSONL alone yields no usable title, sourced from Codex's own state_5.sqlite cache.
expected_behaviour: `apply_rows` (src/integration/codex/sqlite.rs:508-595 (apply_rows, title enrich at 548-555)) only sets `session.sqlite_title` when `session.user_messages.is_empty()` and a matching row has a non-empty title, and always treats `activity_time`/`archived` as additive/enrich-only; `derive_title` in mod.rs only falls back to `sqlite_title` when the JSONL-derived summary is `None` (src/integration/codex/discover.rs:559-567 (derive_title)).
how_to_test: Build with `--features codex-sqlite`, craft a rollout with no usable user messages but a matching state_5.sqlite row with a title, and confirm the picker/--list title reflects the DB title only in that fallback case, never overriding a JSONL-derivable title.

feature_name: Codex SQLite row disagreeing on id/cwd is dropped with a diagnostic, never overrides JSONL identity
user_story: As a Codex user, I want a corrupted or stale state_5.sqlite row that disagrees with the rollout's real id/cwd to be ignored for identity purposes, with a diagnostic so I can notice the inconsistency.
expected_behaviour: `apply_rows` checks `row.id` against `session.id` and `row.cwd` against `session.cwd`; on any disagreement it pushes a `codex_sqlite_id_mismatch`/`codex_sqlite_workspace_mismatch` diagnostic and `continue`s without enriching that session (src/integration/codex/sqlite.rs:516-547 (id check at 525-535, cwd check at 537-547)).
how_to_test: Build with `--features codex-sqlite`, craft a state_5.sqlite row whose id or cwd disagrees with a matching rollout's session_meta, and confirm (a) the session's JSONL-derived identity/workspace are unaffected and (b) a mismatch diagnostic appears with --verbose.
error_notes: Fixed: app discovery now forwards SQLite precedence diagnostics (and degraded enrichment categories) from discover_with_filter_enriched. Verified with the original mismatched state_5.sqlite repro against the fixed all-features release binary: JSONL id/workspace stayed authoritative, the DB title was rejected, and codex_sqlite_id_mismatch appeared in stderr and JSON errors. Phase 4 independent re-test: rebuilt the all-features release binary and replayed the mismatched state_5.sqlite scenario; JSONL ID/workspace remained authoritative, mismatched title was rejected, and codex_sqlite_id_mismatch reached JSON errors and stderr. Fix remains confirmed.

feature_name: Codex SQLite enrichment degrades silently (Absent) when the DB file doesn't exist
user_story: As a Codex user without a state_5.sqlite file (e.g. a fresh Codex install), I want discovery to work identically to the non-enriched path with no warning noise.
expected_behaviour: `enrich()` returns `SqliteOutcome::Absent` immediately when `!db_path.is_file()` (src/integration/codex/sqlite.rs:137-139); `SqliteOutcome::summary()` returns `None` for `Absent`, so no warning is surfaced (src/integration/codex/sqlite.rs:97).
how_to_test: Build with `--features codex-sqlite`, ensure no state_5.sqlite exists under CODEX_HOME, run `resume --list --agent codex`, and confirm output is byte-for-byte identical to the same run without the feature enabled, with no enrichment-related diagnostic.

feature_name: Codex SQLite enrichment degrades to Degraded{corrupt/locked/unsupported_schema} without blocking discovery
user_story: As a Codex user whose state_5.sqlite happens to be corrupted, locked, or has an unrecognized schema, I want Codex session discovery to keep working via JSONL, with at most a coarse warning, never a crash or blocked discovery.
expected_behaviour: `enrich()` classifies `open_readonly`/`detect_schema`/`read_rows` failures into `SqliteOutcome::Degraded { category: "locked"|"corrupt"|"unreadable"|"schema_unreadable"|"unsupported_schema"|"query_failed" }`, always falling back to unmodified JSONL-derived sessions (src/integration/codex/sqlite.rs:140-194); `SqliteOutcome::summary()` renders a `codex_sqlite_degraded: <category> (falling back to JSONL)` line for Degraded outcomes (src/integration/codex/sqlite.rs:118-120).
how_to_test: Build with `--features codex-sqlite`, write a garbage (non-SQLite) file at state_5.sqlite's path, run `resume --list --agent codex`, and confirm Codex sessions still discover correctly from JSONL with no crash (verify the degraded summary is at least computed, even if app.rs doesn't yet surface `SqliteOutcome::summary()` as a diagnostic — check whether app.rs's discover_codex actually surfaces this summary).

feature_name: Codex SQLite is always opened read-only via a URI with mode=ro, never immutable=1 on a live DB
user_story: As a Codex user, I want resume to never risk corrupting or interfering with Codex's own concurrently-written state_5.sqlite.
expected_behaviour: `open_readonly` builds `file:<path>?mode=ro` and opens with `SQLITE_OPEN_READ_ONLY | SQLITE_OPEN_URI | SQLITE_OPEN_NO_MUTEX`, explicitly never `immutable=1` on a live WAL DB (documented rationale at src/integration/codex/sqlite.rs:205-235 (mode=ro URI at 209-213, flags at 222-224)); a `assert_readonly` test helper confirms a write attempt (`CREATE TABLE`) fails on the opened connection (src/integration/codex/sqlite.rs:686-692 (assert_readonly)).
how_to_test: Build with `--features codex-sqlite` and run the crate's own `assert_readonly`-backed test suite (`cargo test --features codex-sqlite`), or independently open the same DB file with the same URI/flags and attempt a write, confirming it's rejected.

feature_name: OMP base config root resolution: PI_CONFIG_DIR overrides default ~/.omp
user_story: As an OMP user with a nondefault base config directory, I want resume to discover sessions relative to PI_CONFIG_DIR when set.
expected_behaviour: `config_root` returns `inputs.config_dir_env.clone()` when set, else `home.join(".omp")` (src/integration/omp/roots.rs:189-198 (fn config_root)).
how_to_test: Set PI_CONFIG_DIR to a custom directory containing omp agent fixtures and confirm `resume --list --agent omp` discovers sessions there.

feature_name: OMP profile selection precedence: internal profile_flag input > OMP_PROFILE > PI_PROFILE (no CLI --profile flag exists)
user_story: As an OMP user with multiple named profiles, I want resume to select the profile using the same precedence OMP itself uses, understanding that today only OMP_PROFILE/PI_PROFILE env vars are reachable — there is no `resume --profile` command-line flag.
expected_behaviour: `select_profile` checks `inputs.profile_flag`, then `inputs.omp_profile_env` (OMP_PROFILE), then `inputs.pi_profile_env` (PI_PROFILE), each requiring a non-whitespace-only value, defaulting to `ProfileSelection::Default` (src/integration/omp/roots.rs:127-144). `profile_flag` is a real, tested field on `ResolutionInputs`, but `ResolutionInputs::from_env()` always sets it to `None` (src/integration/omp/roots.rs:110) and `src/cli.rs` has no `--profile` argument anywhere (0 grep matches) — so in the actual `resume` binary, only the OMP_PROFILE > PI_PROFILE env-var precedence is ever reachable; `profile_flag` exists solely for internal precedence testing.
how_to_test: Run `resume --json --agent omp --profile x` and confirm clap rejects it as an unknown argument (exit 2); set OMP_PROFILE and PI_PROFILE to different names and confirm OMP_PROFILE wins via `resume --json --agent omp`.
error_notes: Corrected 2026-08-11 (parallel real-execution QA sweep): prior feature_name/expected_behaviour implied a working `--profile` CLI flag; verified src/cli.rs has no `profile` argument and `from_env()` hardcodes `profile_flag: None`, so the flag path is untestable from the actual CLI.

feature_name: OMP discovery enumerates the default profile plus every named profile under profiles/
user_story: As an OMP user with several named profiles, I want `resume --list` to surface sessions from all of them at once, not just whichever one is currently selected by env vars.
expected_behaviour: `discover_omp` in app.rs starts with `base_roots` (default/env-selected profile) then reads `base_roots.config_root.join(PROFILES_DIR_NAME)` and resolves an additional `EffectiveRoots` for every named-profile subdirectory found, deduping by `profile` (src/app.rs:570-591 (fn discover_omp, enumeration loop at 575-591)).
how_to_test: Create session fixtures under both the default OMP profile and two named profiles (`profiles/work`, `profiles/personal`), run `resume --list --agent omp`, and confirm sessions from all three appear, each tagged with the correct profile in the agent[profile] display.

feature_name: Named OMP profiles deliberately ignore PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR and XDG_DATA_HOME overrides
user_story: As an OMP user, I want named-profile agent roots to always be `<config-root>/profiles/<name>/agent`, unaffected by env vars that only apply to the unprofiled default.
expected_behaviour: `agent_root` for `ProfileSelection::Named(name)` always returns `config_root.join(PROFILES_DIR_NAME).join(name).join(PROFILE_AGENT_DIR_NAME)`, explicitly bypassing the `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`/`XDG_DATA_HOME` branches that only apply to `ProfileSelection::Default` (src/integration/omp/roots.rs:200-225 (fn agent_root, Named branch at 219-222)), module doc comment: 'named profiles deliberately ignore it.'
how_to_test: Set PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR to some other directory while also having a named OMP profile 'work'; confirm the 'work' profile's sessions are still discovered from `<config-root>/profiles/work/agent`, unaffected by PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR.

feature_name: Default (unprofiled) OMP agent root honors PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR before its own XDG_DATA_HOME/config-root path — deliberately overlapping Pi's root
user_story: As a user who runs both Pi and OMP and has set PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR to a custom location for Pi, I want to understand that OMP's *default profile* will also read sessions from that same directory (since OMP shares Pi's session format by convention), while a *named* OMP profile stays fully isolated from it.
expected_behaviour: `agent_root`'s `ProfileSelection::Default` arm checks `inputs.agent_dir_env` (`PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`) first and returns it directly if set, falling back to `XDG_DATA_HOME` then `<config-root>/agent` only when unset (src/integration/omp/roots.rs:200-216 (fn agent_root, Default branch)); module doc explicitly states this is intentional (src/integration/omp/mod.rs:18: '`PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` overrides only the unprofiled agent root'). Distinct from `omp-named-profile-ignores-pi-coding-agent-dir`, which covers the opposite (named-profile isolation) case.
how_to_test: Set PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR to a directory containing only Pi fixtures (no dedicated OMP fixture); run `resume --json --agent omp` with no profile selected and confirm the reported OMP session's id/title match the Pi fixture's content, not any separate `<config-root>/agent` fixture, because the unprofiled OMP root resolved to the same directory as Pi's.
error_notes: Found during hands-on --json testing 2026-08-11: a combined-fixture test harness setting both PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR (for Pi) and a separate .omp/agent/omp.jsonl produced an 'omp' JSON entry containing Pi's id/title, not the dedicated OMP fixture — confirmed intentional per source, not a bug, but was previously undocumented as its own contract.

feature_name: OMP parses a title sidecar record that may precede the v3 session header, without assuming header position
user_story: As an OMP user, I want resume to correctly read my session's title even though OMP writes a padded title record before the actual session header, unlike Pi's header-first assumption.
expected_behaviour: `find_session_header` scans all records for `type == "session"` rather than assuming position 0 (src/integration/omp/format.rs:240-244 (find_session_header), module doc 'we must not reuse Pi's header-position assumptions'); `extract_session` processes `type == "title"` sidecar records via `TitleState::set` regardless of their position relative to the header (src/integration/omp/mod.rs:139-224 (extract_session)).
how_to_test: Create an OMP session fixture with a `{type:"title", v:1, title:"my title"}` record appearing before the `{type:"session", ...}` header record, and confirm the discovered title is 'my title'.

feature_name: OMP title_change records update the effective title; the latest non-empty title wins
user_story: As an OMP user who renamed a session mid-conversation, I want the picker to show my most recent title, not the original one.
expected_behaviour: `TitleState::set` only overwrites `current` when the new title is non-empty after trim, and records are processed in file order so a later `title_change` naturally overrides an earlier title/header value (src/integration/omp/format.rs:114-124 (TitleState::set), :155-201 (record-order processing in extract_session)).
how_to_test: Create an OMP fixture with an initial header title, followed by a `title_change` record with a different title; confirm the discovered/displayed title is the title_change value, not the original header title.

feature_name: OMP excludes agent/system/tool-attributed messages from the human user-message set
user_story: As an OMP user, I want resume's title/preview summary to be based only on things I actually typed, not on agent-injected or automated content mislabeled with role=user.
expected_behaviour: `is_user_attributed` inspects `attribution.source`/`source`/`meta.source` across record and message_obj, rejecting values `agent|assistant|system|tool|injected|auto|automated`, plus explicit boolean `injected`/`automated` flags (src/integration/omp/format.rs:251-296 (fn is_user_attributed); call site at format.rs:202-211); only messages passing this check are added to `messages` in `extract_session` (src/integration/omp/mod.rs:766-780... actual call site near 'is_user_attributed(record, message_obj)').
how_to_test: Create an OMP fixture with a `message.role="user"` record whose `attribution.source` is `"agent"`, and confirm that message never appears in the derived title/summary, unlike a genuinely user-attributed message.

feature_name: OMP import metadata is exposed only as a safe badge (source kind + short origin id prefix), never the origin path/remote in full
user_story: As an OMP user with sessions imported from Codex/Claude, I want to see that a session was imported and from where in coarse terms, without exposing the full origin session ID or path as a resumable locator.
expected_behaviour: `ImportBadge::to_display` builds `"imported from {source_kind}"` plus, if present, `"origin:<first 8 chars of origin_id>"` — never the full ID, never `origin_cwd` in the display, and the badge is explicitly documented as never merged with the origin session (src/integration/omp/format.rs:29-44 (ImportBadge::to_display); struct at :20-27; parse_import at :315-341, module doc 'Imported Sessions').
how_to_test: Create an OMP fixture with a `foreign_session_import` custom entry with a long `origin_id` and `origin_cwd`; confirm any surfaced import badge shows only the source kind and an 8-character id prefix, never the full id or cwd.
error_notes: Fixed: ParsedSession::into_session appends ImportBadge::to_display to the visible title. Verified with the original isolated OMP import repro against the fixed all-features release binary: title contained imported from codex origin:12345678, while the full origin id and origin_cwd were absent from JSON output.

feature_name: OMP default-profile Resume spec is exactly `omp --resume <id>`
user_story: As an OMP user on the default profile, I want resume's exact resume command to match OMP's own resume mechanism precisely.
expected_behaviour: `resume_spec` for `ProfileSelection::Default` (no `--profile` prefix pushed) builds argv `["--resume", id]`, adding `["--session-dir", root]` only for a custom session root (src/integration/omp/resume.rs:11-29 (resume_spec)).
how_to_test: Resume a default-profile OMP session with a fake `omp` executable that echoes argv and confirm it receives exactly `--resume <id>`.

feature_name: OMP named-profile Resume spec is exactly `omp --profile <name> --resume <id>`
user_story: As an OMP user on a named profile, I want the resume command to explicitly select that profile so I land back in the right isolated OMP context.
expected_behaviour: `resume_spec` prepends `["--profile", name]` before `["--resume", id]` when `roots.profile` is `ProfileSelection::Named(name)` (src/integration/omp/resume.rs:12-16 (Named arm)).
how_to_test: Resume a named-profile ('work') OMP session with a fake `omp` executable and confirm argv is exactly `--profile work --resume <id>`.

feature_name: OMP resume propagates PI_CONFIG_DIR only when it was explicitly set (default root inherited)
user_story: As an OMP user, I want the resumed omp process to resolve the same config/profile root that discovery used whenever I've explicitly customized PI_CONFIG_DIR, but I don't want resume to inject a redundant PI_CONFIG_DIR override for the plain default ~/.omp root, matching how Claude Code and Codex only override their respective env vars for a nondefault root.
expected_behaviour: `resume_env` (src/integration/omp/resume.rs:36-48) returns an empty environment override when `EffectiveRoots.config_root_overridden` is false (the plain ~/.omp default was used), and propagates `PI_CONFIG_DIR = roots.config_root` only when `config_root_overridden` is true (an explicit PI_CONFIG_DIR was set at discovery time), for both default and named profiles. This matches Claude's `resume_spec` (only adds CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR when nondefault) and Codex's `resume_spec` (only adds CODEX_HOME when !is_default_root), closing the asymmetry originally found in QA Phase 2. Regression-tested by `resume_spec_omits_default_config_root_env` and `resume_spec_preserves_explicit_config_root_env` (src/integration/omp/tests.rs).
how_to_test: Resume a default-profile OMP session with a fake omp binary dumping env, using an isolated HOME where PI_CONFIG_DIR was never explicitly set, and confirm PI_CONFIG_DIR is absent from the child environment. Separately resume with PI_CONFIG_DIR explicitly set at discovery time and confirm it IS propagated. Repeat for a named profile.
error_notes: This row originally documented the pre-fix (buggy) unconditional-propagation behavior from QA Phase 1/2, which was exactly the bug fixed in Phase 3 (commit d5aff15, tracked by doccheck-omp-vs-claude-codex-env-propagation-asymmetry). Phase 4 correctly caught that the row's own expected_behaviour contradicted the now-fixed code. Rewrote feature_id/feature_name/user_story/expected_behaviour/how_to_test to describe the corrected conditional-propagation contract and re-verified: integration::omp::tests::resume_spec_omits_default_config_root_env and resume_spec_preserves_explicit_config_root_env both pass.

feature_name: OMP Active status requires a genuine two-stage positive-evidence pipeline with a real staleness gate (M3 fix)
user_story: As an OMP user, I want resume to only claim Active when it has strong, multi-signal evidence (not just a leftover breadcrumb file from a closed terminal).
expected_behaviour: OMP Active is a two-stage positive-evidence pipeline. Stage 1 (`correlate_live_with`, src/integration/omp/activity.rs:169-211): for each terminal breadcrumb it requires (a) a live OMP process on that TTY via `ProcessTable::live_on_tty`, (b) a breadcrumb `recorded_at` (file mtime), and (c) a FRESHNESS GATE — `fresh = recorded_at >= process.started_at` when the process start time is known (activity.rs:183-184); when `started_at` is unavailable it falls back to a 12h window (`now - recorded_at <= BREADCRUMB_FRESHNESS`, :192-193) AND emits an `OMP_BREADCRUMB_START_TIME_UNAVAILABLE` diagnostic so the unknown is visible, never silent. A breadcrumb older than the recycled-TTY process, or older than 12h with no start time, is REJECTED before any evidence is recorded. Stage 2 (`activity_status`/`ActivityEvidence::matches`, activity.rs:19-54): only evidence produced by stage 1 (live_process=true, tty=Some, breadcrumb_alive=true, matching canonical session path) maps to Active; everything else is Unknown. A stale breadcrumb alone can NEVER reach Active because stage 1 never emits evidence for it.
how_to_test: Feed `correlate_live_with` a breadcrumb whose `recorded_at` is older than the live process `started_at` and assert the evidence map is empty (`correlate_live_rejects_breadcrumb_older_than_recycled_tty_process`, src/integration/omp/tests/activity.rs:75). Feed a process with `started_at=None` and a breadcrumb just inside/exactly at the 12h `BREADCRUMB_FRESHNESS` boundary and assert Active + one `OMP_BREADCRUMB_START_TIME_UNAVAILABLE` diagnostic; push `recorded_at` 1s past the boundary and assert empty (`missing_process_start_time_uses_twelve_hour_freshness_fallback`, activity.rs:108). Also assert full positive evidence -> Active and any single missing signal -> Unknown (`correlate_live_requires_process_tty_breadcrumb_and_existing_transcript` :37; `activity_active_only_with_live_process_tty_and_matching_breadcrumb` :227).
error_notes: REWRITTEN — the original row described only the CONSUMER of activity evidence (matches requires live_process+tty+breadcrumb_alive) which was the pre-M3 tautological gate flagged by docs/review/post-merge-review.md finding M3 (a recycled TTY could falsely report Active). The producer-side staleness gate is now real; see the dedicated omp-active-staleness-gate-m3-fix row for the specific exploit-closure evidence.

feature_name: OMP discovery filters sessions by authoritative header cwd against Scope, never directory layout
user_story: As an OMP user, I want scope filtering based on the real recorded working directory in each session, consistent with the other integrations.
expected_behaviour: `discover()` (omp) applies `config.scope.contains_workspace(workspace) (discover.rs:97)` against `parsed.workspace` from the header `cwd`, incrementing `outcome.out_of_scope` when excluded (src/integration/omp/discover.rs:64-92 (fn discover, scope filter at 84-100)), mirroring pi's approach.
how_to_test: Place OMP session fixtures with different header cwd values and confirm Scope filtering (e.g. --up/--down) follows only the header cwd, not the storage directory structure.

feature_name: resume never performs a machine-wide scan; only known integration roots + Scope filtering
user_story: As a user, I want assurance that resume only looks at the specific, documented session-storage locations for enabled agents, never crawling arbitrary parts of my filesystem.
expected_behaviour: Each integration's discovery starts from a resolved, documented root (`~/.pi/agent`, `~/.claude`, `~/.codex`, `~/.omp` or their env overrides) and only recurses within that root's `.jsonl` files (e.g. `collect_jsonl` in src/integration/pi/discover.rs:163 and src/integration/omp/discover.rs:126, `list_rollout_files_into` in src/integration/codex/discover.rs:248, `collect_candidates` in src/integration/claude/discover.rs:78); README.md states this explicitly ('It does not recursively search the machine...').
how_to_test: Run `resume --verbose --list` under `strace`/`dtruss`/`fs_usage` (platform-appropriate) and confirm all directory reads are confined to the resolved agent roots and their subdirectories, never an unrelated filesystem-wide walk.

feature_name: Discovery and Preview never modify session files, mtimes, or directory entries
user_story: As a user, I want resume's read-only discovery/preview to never risk corrupting or altering my agent's session history.
expected_behaviour: All discovery reads go through `jsonl::read_file_confined`/`open_for_read` (src/preview/jsonl.rs:213 / :94), which opens files for read only (`fs::File::open`, never `OpenOptions::write`); `src/preview/snapshot.rs`'s `DirSnapshot` helpers (DirSnapshot at :10-20, snapshot_dir :31, diff_snapshots/assert_unchanged :166-196) exist specifically to regression-test byte/mtime/entry immutability before and after discovery in the integration test suites.
how_to_test: Snapshot a fixture agent root's file bytes/mtimes/directory entries (e.g. via `snapshot_dir`), run `resume --list`/`resume --json` against it, re-snapshot, and confirm the two snapshots are identical.

feature_name: Session-file symlinks are confined to the effective configured root; cross-boundary symlinks are rejected
user_story: As a user, I want a maliciously or accidentally planted symlink inside an agent's session directory pointing outside that root to never be silently followed and surfaced as a 'resumable session'.
expected_behaviour: `jsonl::open_for_read` canonicalizes the target path and rejects it via `io::Error::other(...)` when `!resolved.starts_with(root)` (src/preview/jsonl.rs:90-116 (open_for_read: doc :90-93, fn :94-116, canonicalize :99-103, cross-boundary guard :104-108, rejects via io::Error::other :107)); all four integrations now route production reads through `read_file_confined` with their real effective root, per docs/review/round-2-sonnet-verification.md's verification of the round-1 finding #1 fix (originally flagged in docs/review/round-1-sonnet.md finding #1).
how_to_test: Create a symlink inside e.g. CODEX_HOME/sessions pointing to a file outside CODEX_HOME (a different tempdir), run `resume --list --agent codex`, and confirm the symlinked file's content never surfaces as a session, with a diagnostic reflecting the rejection.
error_notes: Fixed/verified: Codex read_file_confined rejections already became IntegrationError::Io; the real CLI now preserves the diagnostic path through discovery. Re-ran the original cross-boundary symlink repro against the fixed all-features release binary: outside session EVIL did not surface, while codex_io appeared in stderr and JSON errors.

feature_name: Attachments are represented by safe placeholders, never raw base64/pixel/file data
user_story: As a user, I want images/files referenced in my sessions to never have their raw bytes echoed into the picker preview, list output, or JSON.
expected_behaviour: `Attachment::Image`/`Attachment::File` variants carry only `media_type`/`filename` metadata and a static placeholder note (`[image]`/`[file]`), never a data field; `Attachment::to_display` never emits base64, regression-tested by `image_attachment_uses_placeholder_not_base64` and `extract_array_with_text_and_image_blocks`'s comment 'The base64 data is never stored in the attachment' (src/preview/message.rs (Attachment enum :20-30, to_display :55-66, base64-never comment :201)).
how_to_test: Craft a session fixture with an image attachment carrying a large base64 `data` field, and confirm neither `--json` nor the preview pane ever contains that base64 string.

feature_name: Injection filtering collapses only known, complete wrapper tags, never arbitrary user XML/HTML
user_story: As a user, I want my own genuine code or markup containing XML/HTML-like tags to survive display unmangled, while known agent-injected wrappers (like <skill>) are stripped.
expected_behaviour: `collapse_known_injections` only touches tags in `KNOWN_WRAPPERS` (`["skill"]`) and only when fully matched (open+close present); unknown tags, attributed tags (`<skill id="x">`), and incomplete pairs are left untouched (src/preview/injection.rs (KNOWN_WRAPPERS :13, collapse_known_injections :24, tests at :91,102,108,126,131) e.g. `preserves_genuine_xml_tags`, `preserves_unknown_xml_wrappers`, `does_not_match_tag_with_attributes`).
how_to_test: Feed a message containing `<root><child>value</child></root>` alongside a genuine `<skill>injected</skill>` wrapper and confirm only the skill wrapper collapses while the root/child XML is preserved verbatim in the displayed title/preview.

feature_name: All rendered text (rows, preview, titles) is stripped of ANSI/CSI/OSC/C1/bidi control sequences
user_story: As a user, I want a session containing malicious ANSI escape sequences (e.g. a fake OSC 8 hyperlink, terminal title hijack, or bidi-override filename spoofing) in its content to never be able to manipulate my terminal when displayed.

feature_name: Three-layer help design (-h short / --help full reference / --man manual)

Per-arg, only `help` is set (never `long_help`), keeping the `--help` option column scannable; long prose lives only in the man page. clap's rule: when `long_about`/`after_long_help` are set, `--help` uses them and `-h` falls back to `about`/`after_help`. error_notes: E2E GAP: help_describes_every_option (src/cli.rs:391) renders ONLY render_long_help() (the --help layer). No test renders render_help() (the -h layer) to assert it is strictly shorter and uses about/after_help not long_about/after_long_help. The strict-subset invariant is documented but not automated. feature_name: Unified E-code error catalog (E1001-E1004/E3001-E3003) — single source of truth, selectively wired
user_story: As a user/debugger, I want stable E-codes (E1001 INVALID_SINCE ... E3003 WORKSPACE_UNAVAILABLE) with consistent trigger/fix/example text across stderr, --help, and --man, so I can grep/Google a code and get an actionable remedy.
expected_behaviour: `src/errors.rs` defines `CATALOG: [ErrorSpec; 7]` as the single source; `Report::emit()` writes a four-line block (`ERROR [Exxxx] SLUG: <what>` / `Trigger:` / `Fix:` / `Example:`) to stderr and returns the exit code. Wiring is PARTIAL and indirect: E1001 (INVALID_SINCE) and E1003 (INVALID_DISTANCE) are wired only as the parser-hint STRING (cli.rs:49,21 via `.parser_message()`), wrapped in clap's own value-parse error format — the four-line block is NOT emitted for these. E1002 (CONFLICTING_DIRECTION) has NO runtime emit site at all — the --up/--down mutual exclusion is enforced by clap's `conflicts_with` attribute, which emits clap's generic ArgumentConflict text instead. E1004 (INVALID_CONFIG) IS wired via the four-line block (app.rs:98-104). E1005 (UNKNOWN_AGENT) and E3004 (DIRECTORY_UNREADABLE) are RESERVED but not wired by design (errors.rs doc comment lines 15-18) — those paths still print bare `resume: <message>`. main.rs has ZERO errors:: references; Cli::validate() (cli.rs:346-369) uses plain clap ArgumentConflict text with no E-code for the --list/--json+confirm and config/completions+query rejections.
how_to_test: `resume --up 1 --down 2` (exit 2, clap conflict text — NOT the E1002 four-line block); `resume --since yesterday` (exit 2, message contains the E1001 parser-hint string); `resume --up -1` (exit 2, E1003 hint string); `resume --config /bad.toml --list` (exit 2, four-line E1004 block); `resume --list --confirm-always` (exit 2, clap ArgumentConflict plain text, no E-code).
error_notes: KEY ASYMMETRY: the four-line Report block is emitted ONLY from app.rs (E1004, E3003) — never from cli.rs or main.rs. The man page (man.rs:60, 463) implies the user will see an E1002-branded block for --up/--down conflicts, but they will not; this is a latent doc/behavior mismatch worth a future decision (wire E1002 via a custom conflict handler, or soften the man/help wording). Tests: errors.rs unit tests pin catalog internal consistency; man.rs:629 pins man<->catalog sync. No test asserts which runtime paths do vs don't emit the four-line block.

feature_name: OMP Active detection staleness gate closes the recycled-TTY false-positive (M3 fix)
user_story: As an OMP user, I want resume to never falsely report a session Active just because a leftover terminal breadcrumb names its path while a DIFFERENT, newer process now owns that recycled TTY — a stale breadcrumb must be rejected against the live process's actual start time.
expected_behaviour: `correlate_live_with` (src/integration/omp/activity.rs:169-211) reads each breadcrumb's `recorded_at` (file mtime, :180-182) and the live process's `started_at` (ProcEntry.started_at, src/proc.rs:35). It rejects the breadcrumb unless fresh: when `started_at` is known, `recorded_at >= started_at` (activity.rs:183-184) — so a breadcrumb written by a PREVIOUS process on that TTY, older than the current process, is dropped. When `started_at` is unavailable it falls back to a 12h `BREADCRUMB_FRESHNESS` window (:192-193) and emits an `OMP_BREADCRUMB_START_TIME_UNAVAILABLE` diagnostic (errors::category::OMP_BREADCRUMB_START_TIME_UNAVAILABLE) so the unknown is surfaced rather than silently trusted. This replaced the pre-fix gate, which was a tautology/no-op: it only checked a `breadcrumb_alive` boolean set without any time comparison, so any recycled-TTY breadcrumb with a live process and matching path falsely reported Active.
how_to_test: Regression test `correlate_live_rejects_breadcrumb_older_than_recycled_tty_process` (src/integration/omp/tests/activity.rs:75): breadcrumb recorded_at = EPOCH, process started_at = EPOCH+1s -> evidence map empty (the exploit is closed). Regression test `missing_process_start_time_uses_twelve_hour_freshness_fallback` (activity.rs:108): started_at=None, breadcrumb at exactly BREADCRUMB_FRESHNESS ago -> Active + 1 diagnostic; 1s older -> empty.

user_story: As a tool author consuming resume --json, I want the errors[] array to expose one aggregated entry per category with a summed count, not N raw per-occurrence entries, so counts are stable and match stderr.
expected_behaviour: `print_json` (src/app.rs:814) calls `aggregate_diagnostics(&errors_guard, false)` at src/app.rs:838 BEFORE constructing the `JsonError` list — collapsing same-category occurrences into one entry with a summed count, the same function `print_diagnostics` uses for stderr. Pre-fix, `print_json` iterated `state.errors` raw, so three malformed transcripts in the same category produced three duplicate-keyed JSON entries instead of one aggregated entry.
how_to_test: Force 3 same-category diagnostics (e.g. 3 corrupt codex transcripts), run `resume --json --agent codex`; confirm errors[] has ONE entry with count 3, and that count equals the stderr 'category: 3' line for the same run.
error_notes: M5 fix (docs/review/post-merge-review.md). Dedicated multi-category regression coverage added: json_errors_aggregate_counts_match_stderr_across_multiple_categories (tests/step9_app.rs) forces 2 codex_invalid_session and 2 claude_no_session_id diagnostics in the same run, asserts each category collapses to exactly one JSON errors[] entry with count 2, and that stderr's 'category: 2' lines match -- proving aggregation is per-category, not a single global collapse. Prior incidental coverage (codex_corrupt_rollout_is_diagnosed_while_valid_sibling_survives, tests/step9_app.rs:230-238) remains single-category.

feature_name: Selecting a non-Supported Session now emits the unified four-line E3003 WORKSPACE_UNAVAILABLE block (exit code unchanged at 2)
user_story: As a user who selects a session resume cannot safely resume, I want a consistent, actionable four-line error explaining why, not a bare one-line message.
expected_behaviour: `resume_selected`'s support guard (src/app.rs:312-321) now calls `crate::errors::E3003.report(...).emit()` instead of a bare `EXIT_USAGE` return. `E3003` (WORKSPACE_UNAVAILABLE, src/errors.rs:164-170) has `exit_code: 2` — identical to the old EXIT_USAGE constant — so the user-observable exit code is UNCHANGED; only the internal mechanism and stderr formatting moved to the unified four-line catalog block.
how_to_test: Select a DiscoverOnly or Unavailable session via the picker (or construct one directly) and confirm the four-line ERROR [E3003] WORKSPACE_UNAVAILABLE block prints to stderr with exit code 2.
error_notes: Cross-cuts launch-revalidate-unsupported. Test: report_carries_its_spec_and_exit_code (src/errors.rs:460) asserts E3003.exit_code()==2 at the Report level. Dedicated coverage of the resume_selected dispatch itself added: resume_selected_reports_e3003_for_every_non_supported_status (src/app.rs) drives resume_selected directly with Unsupported, DiscoverOnly, and Unavailable sessions, plus a Supported session missing its ResumeSpec/LaunchEvidence, and asserts every branch returns E3003.exit_code (2) -- proving the function actually reaches the E3003 report instead of falling through toward launch::exec. The literal four-line stderr text is exercised by errors.rs's Display/emit tests, not reproduced again here to avoid duplicating that assertion.

feature_name: TITLE/WORKSPACE column budget adapts to terminal width (16-60 cols, default 48 with no TTY)
user_story: As a user piping resume --list output through a script or redirecting to a file, I want the title column width to be stable regardless of terminal state, per docs/product-design.md's documented bounds.
expected_behaviour: `title_column_width` (src/app.rs:676-694) clamps the computed width to [TITLE_WIDTH_MIN=16, TITLE_WIDTH_MAX=60] and falls back to TITLE_WIDTH_DEFAULT (48) when there is no controlling terminal (the common case for --list/--json in tests, CI, and redirected/piped invocations).
how_to_test: Run `resume --list` with no controlling terminal (e.g. in CI or with output redirected) and confirm the title column is exactly the documented default width.
error_notes: Test: title_column_width_stays_within_documented_bounds (src/app.rs:1002).

feature_name: PreviewPosition::Auto picks right (wide terminal) vs bottom (narrow terminal)
user_story: As a user without an explicit preview_position preference, I want resume to automatically choose a sensible preview layout based on my terminal width.
expected_behaviour: `build_production_options` (src/picker.rs:395-402) maps PreviewPosition::Auto to "right" when `tty_size()` width >= 100, else "down" (bottom); Right/Bottom map directly without the width check.
how_to_test: In a wide terminal (>=100 cols) with preview_position=auto, confirm the preview renders on the right; in a narrower terminal, confirm it renders at the bottom.
error_notes: Verified by manual/PTY testing per config-preview-position-field's error_notes; no isolated automated unit test for the Auto-width-threshold branch specifically (E2E gap, low priority).

feature_name: Pi discovery parses v1, v2, and v3 session headers identically
user_story: As a Pi user with older session files, I want resume to discover sessions regardless of which Pi header version produced them.
expected_behaviour: `extract_session` finds the first record with `type=="session"` and extracts id/cwd/parentSession/timestamp regardless of the version field; v1/v2/v3 are field-compatible (src/integration/pi/discover.rs:213-271, find_session_header at :273-276).
how_to_test: Write three fixtures with type="session" headers tagged version 1, 2, and 3 respectively (same id/cwd); confirm all three discover successfully.
error_notes: Tests: parses_v3_header_extracts_id_and_workspace (pi/tests/format.rs:20), parses_v2_header_same_shape_as_v3 (:40), parses_v1_header_uses_id_field (:56).

feature_name: Pi activity_time uses message timestamps, then header, then file mtime
user_story: As a Pi user, I want session recency to reflect real activity, falling back gracefully when timestamps are sparse.
expected_behaviour: ParsedSession.activity_time = latest_message_time.or(header_time).or(file_mtime) (src/integration/pi/discover.rs:259-261).
how_to_test: Write a session with user-message timestamps newer than the header; confirm activity_time follows the message. Write one with only a header timestamp; confirm it follows the header. Write one with no timestamps; confirm it falls back to file mtime.
error_notes: Test: activity_time_prefers_message_then_header_then_mtime (pi/tests/discover.rs:218).

feature_name: Pi discovery dedupes sessions by canonical transcript path under the effective session root
user_story: As a Pi user with symlinked or aliased session files, I want resume to show each real session only once.
expected_behaviour: discover() canonicalizes each jsonl_path and dedupes by (session_root, canonical_path); the same id under different roots yields distinct sessions (src/integration/pi/discover.rs:108-124).
how_to_test: Create two symlinks to the same transcript under the same session root; confirm only one session appears. Create the same id under two different session roots; confirm both appear as distinct.
error_notes: Tests: duplicate_files_under_same_root_are_deduped (pi/tests/discover.rs:93), same_id_across_different_roots_are_distinct (:164).

feature_name: Pi discovery tolerates malformed middle records and truncated tails without aborting
user_story: As a Pi user with a partially-corrupt session file, I want resume to salvage valid records rather than skipping the whole file.
expected_behaviour: The shared jsonl reader skips malformed middle records (counted in read.malformed_middle) and marks incomplete tails as IncompleteTail; extract_session retains all valid records parsed before the corruption (src/integration/pi/discover.rs:213-271).
how_to_test: Write a session jsonl with a valid header, a malformed JSON line in the middle, and a valid user message after it; confirm the session still discovers with the valid message.
error_notes: Tests: malformed_middle_record_does_not_abort_discovery (pi/tests/discover.rs:264), truncated_tail_is_incomplete_but_keeps_valid_records (:290).

feature_name: Claude user-message extraction excludes tool_result blocks and injected (isMeta/isSidechain) records from the title summary
user_story: As a Claude Code user, I want session titles to reflect what I actually typed, not tool output or agent-injected sidechain content.
expected_behaviour: interpret_record only treats type="user" records with non-tool_result content and !isMeta/!isSidechain as human input (src/integration/claude/format.rs:100-121, has_human_input :123-137, is_injected :139-148).
how_to_test: Write a transcript with a user record containing only tool_result blocks; confirm it does not contribute to the title. Write one with isMeta=true; confirm it is excluded.
error_notes: Tests: user_record_with_only_tool_result_blocks_is_excluded_from_title (claude/tests/format.rs:224), mixed_text_and_tool_result_blocks_extract_human_text_only (:258), assistant_system_and_injected_records_excluded_from_user_messages (:290).

feature_name: Claude discovery never modifies any file, directory, or mtime
user_story: As a Claude Code user, I want resume's discovery to be purely read-only so it cannot corrupt my session store.
expected_behaviour: discover() and collect_candidates only read directories and open files for reading; no file is opened for write, no directory entry or mtime is changed (src/integration/claude/discover.rs:37-41 doc comment).
how_to_test: Snapshot all file mtimes and contents under a Claude config root before and after `resume --list --agent claude`; confirm zero changes.
error_notes: Test: discovery_does_not_modify_any_file_or_directory (claude/tests/discover.rs:329).

feature_name: Claude discovery emits claude_truncated, claude_oversized, and claude_malformed non-fatal diagnostics while retaining valid sessions
user_story: As a Claude Code user diagnosing with --verbose, I want to know when a transcript was truncated, oversized, or had malformed middle records, without losing the session entirely.
expected_behaviour: parse_candidate pushes nonfatal diagnostics for IncompleteTail (claude_truncated), BoundExceeded (claude_oversized), and malformed_middle > 0 (claude_malformed), but still returns Some(session) (src/integration/claude/format.rs:268-289).
how_to_test: Write a transcript ending mid-JSON-line; confirm claude_truncated appears and the session is retained. Write one exceeding the read bound; confirm claude_oversized. Write one with a malformed middle line; confirm claude_malformed.
error_notes: Tests: truncated_incomplete_tail_is_diagnosed_but_session_retained (claude/tests/format.rs:341), malformed_middle_record_is_diagnosed_but_not_aborted (:375).

feature_name: Git common-dir lookup is memoized per canonical Workspace (performance contract)
user_story: As a user resuming inside a large repo with many sessions, I want resume to query each Workspace's git common directory at most once, so discovery stays fast rather than spawning one git subprocess per session.
expected_behaviour: In ScopeMode::Git, Scope::contains_workspace resolves git_common_dir via cached_git_common_dir (src/scope.rs:155-179), keyed by canonical path, shared via Arc<Scope> across per-agent threads. Non-Git modes skip the spawn entirely (src/scope.rs:142).
how_to_test: Run contains_workspace against the same canonical path repeatedly and confirm only the first call spawns git.
error_notes: Test: contains_workspace_memoizes_git_common_dir_per_canonical_path (src/scope.rs) asserts the second batch of identical-path calls is >=5x faster than the first. Implements docs/product-design.md §4 'Query each normalized Workspace at most once.'

feature_name: A Session whose Workspace was deleted is still Scope-matched via its last-known real path
user_story: As a user, I want a session recorded under a now-deleted directory to still be matched by Scope (so it appears, marked Unavailable) rather than silently vanishing from the list.
expected_behaviour: resolve_missing_workspace_path (src/scope.rs:198-219) canonicalizes the nearest existing ancestor and re-appends the missing suffix; contains_workspace falls back to it when canonicalize fails (src/scope.rs:136-150).
how_to_test: Discover a session under /real/base/deleted (base exists, deleted subdir does not); confirm it is still matched under --down all, while an unrelated /other/deleted path is not.
error_notes: Test: missing_workspace_uses_its_last_known_path_for_scope_matching (src/scope.rs). Distinct from scope-unavailable-workspace (which marks availability); this row pins the Scope-membership contract for deleted paths.

feature_name: Config parse errors report file path, line/column, and offending field
user_story: As a user with a typo in config.toml, I want the error to name the file, line, and field so I can fix it without guessing.
expected_behaviour: ConfigError::Parse interpolates {source} (the toml::de::Error Display carrying line/column + field) alongside {path:?} (src/config.rs:56-60), so the message includes 'line 1' and the field name.
how_to_test: Write config.toml containing `mystery = true`; run `resume --config <path> --list`; confirm the error contains 'line 1' and 'mystery'.
error_notes: Test: parse_error_message_includes_line_and_field_detail (src/config.rs:158). Implements docs/product-design.md §7 'errors with file/line/column when possible.'
